doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Miles, Monk and the New York circle
title: Miles Davis invites him to join the band
summary: Lloyd says Miles came to hear him nightly, invited him to join between George Coleman and Wayne Shorter, but Lloyd stayed with Cannonball; Crouch's remark and Miles's book.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: I mean, the art, if we go back fifty years...
Yeah
You were the one that set the pathway, and opened the door for all of the people. I'm thinking of Miles and many others that came after you because you laid down the blueprint.
Well they influenced me too. I heard Miles early on and that influenced me, but I will say this about what you're saying: Whenever and where I would play, Miles would be there.
Yeah

And he also wanted me to play in his band, he invited me to play in his band, but the problem with that was I just joined Cannonball. He was there every night that he and I were playing Cannonball, and he asked me "When you going to bring your music up to my house, I want to see what you're writing." We were talking about doing something, he wanted me to join his band that was before Wayne came I think he had...
George Coleman?
No it was after George. He had Sam Rivers..
Oh yeah...
It was during the period I was with Cannon, it was a transition period.
Right.

And he was groping, and when Wayne came he was fine. He said to me "What do you think?" I said, “Sam It's great, it don't fit with you so well but he's a great player.” Cause Tony loved him; they came from Boston.
Yeah, yeah.
And he said "Why won't you come and join the band?" I said “Man, I just got with Cannon and it would be against a trust.” Cannon had a vision, and think it was gonna be a year and a half.
Yeah.
Plus I knew the fact that Miles's could be a different bunch of guys.
[laughs]

And he had a different side too that I didn't want to experience. I remember once Crouch, Sandler Crouch was talking with me, and he said "If you had gone with Miles, that wouldn't have worked." I said "Why is that?" He said "Cause when the women come around, he would get upset."
[laughs]
He said "Miles wouldn't want no competition with that stuff."
That's true.

But my point was, I loved Miles and we would hang out, he cooked for me, he's a great cook. He cooks fish and some greens and all kinds of stuff, and was really interested in my music. But then in his book he said I couldn't play and stuff, I had a sign. But you know, he's like a bunch of different guys, and he was always on my case about coming to play with him, but I never did it.
Mmhmm.
